questions.text: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.explanation: Canberra was chosen as the capital in 1908 as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.

questions.text: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.explanation: Mars appears red due to iron oxide (rust) on its surface.

questions.text: What is the largest mammal in the world?
questions.explanation: Blue whales can reach 30 meters in length and weigh up to 180 tonnes.

questions.text: In which year did the first iPhone release?
questions.explanation: The original iPhone was announced in January 2007 and released in June 2007.

questions.text: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.explanation: Au comes from the Latin 'aurum', meaning gold.
The Pacific Ocean covers about 63 million square miles.

questions.text: What is the hardest natural substance on Earth?
questions.explanation: Diamond scores 10 on the Mohs hardness scale.
The seven continents: Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Europe, North America, Oceania, South America.

questions.text: What is the speed of light in vacuum?
questions.explanation: Light travels at approximately 299,792,458 meters per second.
Hydrogen is the lightest and most abundant element in the universe.

questions.text: What is the largest organ in the human body?
questions.explanation: The skin is the body's largest organ by surface area and weight.

questions.text: Which country has the most islands?
questions.explanation: Canada has over 52,000 islands, more than any other country.

questions.text: What year did World War II end?
questions.explanation: WWII ended in 1945 with Germany surrendering in May and Japan in September.

questions.text: What is the main component of the Sun?
questions.explanation: The Sun is about 73% hydrogen and 25% helium by mass.
